claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

First, let me ask: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you enquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm inquiring about my son Alex - he's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you're inquiring about your son Alex who is 11 years old.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to ask:

**Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or towards his accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially - I contribute towards his clothes, school things, and general upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. To determine your eligibility, I need to understand the amount you're contributing:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)?**

For reference, the current Child Benefit rate is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child (and £16.95 per week for additional children).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum, but she's not claiming Child Benefit for him - no one is claiming it at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just clarify one final point:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, in care, or in residential accommodation for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, that's important information. I need to understand this better:

**How long has Alex been in hospital, and do you regularly spend money on him while he's there (for example, on clothes, treats, toys, or other items for him)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for about 15 weeks now. As for spending money on him while he's there... I'm not sure what you mean exactly - do you mean beyond the weekly contribution I already make?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's what I mean. Let me clarify:

When a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you can still be entitled to Child Benefit if you regularly spend money directly on the child (such as buying them clothes, treats, toys, books, or other personal items for them while they're in hospital).

**So, in addition to or as part of your £50 weekly contribution, are you regularly spending money on items specifically for Alex - such as clothes, treats, toys, or other personal things for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: To be honest, I'm not really sure. I mean, I give the money to his mum for his upkeep, but I don't know exactly what gets spent on him or whether she's buying him things while he's in hospital.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. Let me ask a few more clarifying questions:

**1. Are you yourself directly purchasing any items for Alex (such as clothes, toys, books, etc.) that you give to him or that are for his use, separate from the money you give to his mum?**

**2. Also, is Alex in a hospital here in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
1. No, I don't buy things for him directly myself - I just give the money to his mum for his upkeep.

2. Yes, he's in a hospital here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have enough information now to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex doesn't live with you, but you contribute £50 per week towards his upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- However, Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks (more than 12 weeks)

The issue here is that when a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you can continue to be entitled to Child Benefit only if you regularly spend money directly on them. Since you give money to Alex's mum but don't know if it's being spent on Alex while he's in hospital, and you're not directly purchasing items for Alex yourself, it's unclear whether you meet this exception to the 12-week hospital rule.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**My Assessment:** Your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex is **indeterminate** at this stage.

Here's why:

✓ You meet several key requirements:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- You contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is well above the Child Benefit rate
- No one else is claiming for Alex

✗ However, there's a complicating factor:
- Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks, which exceeds the 12-week threshold
- After 12 weeks in hospital, you can only continue to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money **on the child directly**
- Since you give money to Alex's mum but don't know what it's spent on, and you don't buy things for Alex yourself, it's unclear whether you meet this exception

**What I'd recommend:** You should contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific situation. You may need to provide evidence that your contributions are being used for Alex's personal needs while he's in hospital, or you could start purchasing items directly for Alex (clothes, treats, books, etc.) to demonstrate regular spending on him. HMRC can assess your individual circumstances and determine if you qualify under the hospital exception.
